profile.summary: RoseTTAFoldNA (also called RF2NA) predicts the three-dimensional structure of proteins, RNA and DNA, alone or bound together in complexes. It takes the sequence of each chain, builds multiple sequence alignments and template searches, and outputs an atomic model in PDB format with per-residue confidence (predicted lDDT) and predicted aligned error. It extends the RoseTTAFold protein structure network to nucleic acids.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; README: Inputs, Expected outputs

summary_quotes.text: Here we extend the RoseTTAFold machine learning protein-structure-prediction approach to additionally predict nucleic acid and protein–nucleic acid complexes.
We develop a single trained network, RoseTTAFoldNA, that rapidly produces three-dimensional structure models with confidence estimates for protein–DNA and protein–RNA complexes.
The remaining arguments are fasta files for individual chains in the structure.
You will get a predicted structre with estimated per-residue LDDT in the B-factor column (`models/model_00.pdb`)
pae (L x L) - the per-residue pair predicted error

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RoseTTAFoldNA uses the three-track design of RoseTTAFold, which refines three representations together: the sequence (1D), pairwise distances between residues (2D) and atom coordinates (3D). The authors extended each track to nucleic acids. The 1D track gains 10 tokens for the four DNA and four RNA nucleotides plus unknown DNA and unknown RNA. The 2D track models base-base and base-amino acid interactions. The 3D track places each nucleotide with a frame on its phosphate group and 10 torsion angles. The network has 36 three-track layers and four refinement layers. It was trained on protein monomers and complexes, RNA monomers and dimers, and protein-RNA and protein-DNA complexes from the PDB, with a generalised all-atom FAPE loss, and inputs include MSAs of related protein and nucleic acid sequences.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, paragraphs on architecture (Fig. 1) and training

quotes.text: It is based on the three-track architecture of RoseTTAFold
which simultaneously refines three representations of a biomolecular system: sequence (1D), residue-pair distances (2D) and cartesian coordinates (3D).
we added 10 additional tokens, corresponding to the four DNA nucleotides, the four RNA nucleotides, unknown DNA and unknown RNA.
we generalized the 2D track to model interactions between nucleic acid bases and between bases and amino acids.
using a coordinate frame describing the position and orientation of the phosphate group (P, OP1 and OP2), and 10 torsion angles
RoseTTAFoldNA consists of 36 of these three-track layers, followed by four additional structure refinement layers

We trained this end-to-end protein–NA structure prediction network using a combination of protein monomers, protein complexes, RNA monomers, RNA dimers, protein–RNA complexes and protein–DNA complexes
sequence similarity searches were used to generate multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) of related protein and nucleic acid molecules.
a generalization of the all atom Frame Aligned Point Error (FAPE) loss

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The README lists v0.2, dated 13 April 2023, with updated weights (RF2NA_apr23.tgz) for better homodimer-DNA prediction and DNA sequence recognition, MSA pipeline bug fixes and support for paired protein/RNA MSAs. The run script loads network/weights/RF2NA_apr23.pt. The sources do not say which weights the paper's results used. Predictions also depend on the sequence and template databases, which the README downloads at fixed versions for UniRef30 (2020_06) and the PDB templates (pdb100_2021Mar03) but from the current release for Rfam and RNAcentral. A result should name the weights file, the repository commit (this page read f761af28) and the database versions.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Structure prediction network for proteins, nucleic acids and protein-nucleic acid complexes.

quotes.text: RoseTTAFoldNA extends the RoseTTAFold2 platform to predict the structures of protein–DNA and protein–RNA complexes.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: RoseTTAFold three-track network (1D sequence, 2D pair, 3D coordinates) extended to nucleic acids: 36 three-track layers plus four structure refinement layers. The repository includes NVIDIA's SE(3)-Transformer.

quotes.text: RoseTTAFoldNA consists of 36 of these three-track layers, followed by four additional structure refinement layers
You also need to install NVIDIA's SE(3)-Transformer

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: One FASTA file per chain, tagged P (protein), R (RNA), D (double-stranded DNA, complementary strand generated automatically), S (single-stranded DNA) or PR (paired protein/RNA). The pipeline builds protein MSAs with HHblits, searches templates with hhsearch, and builds RNA MSAs with a reduced rMSA, against local databases.

quotes.text: Use the tags `P:xxx.fa` `R:xxx.fa` `D:xxx.fa` `S:xxx.fa` to specify protein, RNA, double-stranded DNA, and single-stranded DNA, respectively.
Use the tag `PR:xxx.fa` to specify paired protein/RNA.
'D' will automatically generate a complementary DNA strand to the input strand.
echo "Running HHblits"
echo "Running hhsearch"
echo "Running rMSA (lite)"

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: models/model_00.pdb with predicted per-residue lDDT in the B-factor column, and models/model_00.npz holding the predicted distogram (L x L x 37), per-residue predicted lDDT (L) and predicted aligned error (L x L).

quotes.text: You will get a predicted structre with estimated per-residue LDDT in the B-factor column (`models/model_00.pdb`)
dist (L x L x 37) - the predicted distogram
lddt (L) - the per-residue predicted lddt
pae (L x L) - the per-residue pair predicted error

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Structures from the PDB determined before May 2020: protein monomers and complexes, RNA monomers and dimers, and protein-RNA and protein-DNA complexes, at a 60/40 ratio of protein-only to nucleic-acid-containing examples. After clustering there were 1,632 RNA clusters and 1,556 protein-nucleic acid complex clusters. 580 protein-DNA complexes were also used with padded and mutated DNA for sequence-specificity training.

quotes.text: We trained the model using structures determined prior to May 2020
with a 60/40 ratio of protein-only and NA-containing structures
there are 1,632 RNA clusters and 1,556 protein–nucleic acid complex clusters compared to 26,128 all protein clusters
This yielded 580 protein–DNA complexes.

facts.value: PDB structures determined before May 2020; structures solved since then were used as an independent validation set.

quotes.text: We trained the model using structures determined prior to May 2020, and used RNA and protein–NA structures solved since then as an additional independent validation set.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Training examples were cropped to 256 residues or nucleotides. For validation, complexes above 1,000 amino acids and nucleotides were excluded because of GPU memory. The sources do not state a hard limit at inference.

quotes.text: Examples larger than 256 residues/nucleotides in length were ‘cropped’ to 256 residues in length.
Due to GPU memory limitations, for the validation set only, we excluded complexes with more than 1,000 total amino acids and nucleotides

run_guide.summary: Install RoseTTAFold2NA and its databases, then predict the structure of the README's example protein-RNA complex.
prerequisites: Linux with conda; the environment file pins python=3.10, pytorch-cuda=11.7 and a CUDA 11.7 build of DGL. GPU type and memory are not stated.
Several hundred gigabytes of disk for the databases: UniRef30 [46G], BFD [272G], nt [151G], RNAcentral [12G], Rfam [300M] and the PDB templates.
The run script uses 8 CPUs and up to 64 GB memory for the MSA tools.
Code is MIT licensed; no licence is stated for the weights.

steps.title: Download the sequence and structure databases
steps.shell:
# uniref30 [46G]
wget http://wwwuser.gwdg.de/~compbiol/uniclust/2020_06/UniRef30_2020_06_hhsuite.tar.gz
mkdir -p UniRef30_2020_06
tar xfz UniRef30_2020_06_hhsuite.tar.gz -C ./UniRef30_2020_06

# BFD [272G]
wget https://bfd.mmseqs.com/bfd_metaclust_clu_complete_id30_c90_final_seq.sorted_opt.tar.gz
mkdir -p bfd
tar xfz bfd_metaclust_clu_complete_id30_c90_final_seq.sorted_opt.tar.gz -C ./bfd

# structure templates (including *_a3m.ffdata, *_a3m.ffindex)
wget https://files.ipd.uw.edu/pub/RoseTTAFold/pdb100_2021Mar03.tar.gz
tar xfz pdb100_2021Mar03.tar.gz

# RNA databases
mkdir -p RNA
cd RNA

# Rfam [300M]
wget ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Rfam/CURRENT/Rfam.full_region.gz
wget ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/Rfam/CURRENT/Rfam.cm.gz
gunzip Rfam.cm.gz
cmpress Rfam.cm

# RNAcentral [12G]
wget ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/RNAcentral/current_release/rfam/rfam_annotations.tsv.gz
wget ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/RNAcentral/current_release/id_mapping/id_mapping.tsv.gz
wget ftp://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/RNAcentral/current_release/sequences/rnacentral_species_specific_ids.fasta.gz
../input_prep/reprocess_rnac.pl id_mapping.tsv.gz rfam_annotations.tsv.gz   # ~8 minutes
gunzip -c rnacentral_species_specific_ids.fasta.gz | makeblastdb -in - -dbtype nucl  -parse_seqids -out rnacentral.fasta -title "RNACentral"

# nt [151G]
update_blastdb.pl --decompress nt
cd ..
steps.explanation: Downloads and prepares the databases used for MSAs and templates, run from the repository root as in the README. Rfam and RNAcentral come from their current releases, so they change over time.

quotes.text: tar xfz UniRef30_2020_06_hhsuite.tar.gz -C ./UniRef30_2020_06
tar xfz bfd_metaclust_clu_complete_id30_c90_final_seq.sorted_opt.tar.gz -C ./bfd
tar xfz pdb100_2021Mar03.tar.gz
gunzip Rfam.cm.gz cmpress Rfam.cm

gunzip -c rnacentral_species_specific_ids.fasta.gz | makeblastdb -in - -dbtype nucl  -parse_seqids -out rnacentral.fasta -title "RNACentral"
update_blastdb.pl --decompress nt

steps.title: Predict a protein-RNA complex
steps.shell:
conda activate RF2NA
cd example
../run_RF2NA.sh rna_pred rna_binding_protein.fa R:RNA.fa
steps.explanation: Runs the README's protein/RNA example. The first argument is the output folder; the protein FASTA has no tag and the RNA FASTA is tagged R.

quotes.text: conda activate RF2NA cd example # run Protein/RNA prediction ../run_RF2NA.sh rna_pred rna_binding_protein.fa R:RNA.fa
The first argument to the script is the output folder

outputs: In the output folder rna_pred, a models subfolder holding model_00.pdb (predicted lDDT in the B-factor column) and model_00.npz with the distogram, per-residue lDDT and PAE tables. The run script prints "Done" at the end.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The database downloads take several hundred gigabytes and some use FTP links to current releases, which may have moved or changed.
The README's protein/DNA example is the same command with D:DNA.fa and output folder dna_pred.

notes: The record is named RosettaFoldNA; the paper calls the model RoseTTAFoldNA (RFNA) and the repository calls it RF2NA (RoseTTAFold2 with nucleic acids). The paper does not say which weights its results used; the README links the April 2023 v0.2 weights.
